review_method.actual_tools: view_image on all five actual decoded-MP4 chronological contact sheets and all five actual aligned comparison PNGs
review_method.limitations: Chronological full-frame sampling reveals jump/flicker/order issues but is not a native-rate real-time playback session.

territory.continuity: Purple advances northward through the whole clip while orange contracts at the same shared seam; no newly appearing disconnected control patch, duplicate-color acquired band, hard wipe or reversal observed in any contact frame. Actual geographic islands remain part of the supplied native land geometry.
territory.opacity: Both fills retain visible underlying relief. Existing and newly acquired purple now read as one continuous information region.
territory.contrast: Orange/red and purple are immediately distinct in every aligned comparison.
territory.reference_gap: Current measured 64-knot frontier is visibly coarser and more angular than the reference fine irregular seam, especially its west-side turns and end ridge. Exact reference shape parity is not established.

frontier.alignment: Thin warm-pale luminous edge visually follows the current orange/purple ownership seam throughout all five chronological sheets and all five aligned checkpoints; it does not become a detached guide line.
frontier.coherence: Terrain, territorial fill, seam and world-anchored units remain spatially coherent through pan/zoom/roll.
frontier.brightness: Restrained center light has no observed large flash or thick neon bloom. At small phone/contact-sheet scale the luminous edge is subtle; region color change provides the strongest direction cue.
frontier.pixel_width: Scene profile center 1.4 output px and finite halo support 7.5 output px; this review does not claim an independent photometric pixel-width measurement.

units_and_occlusion.layout: Unit positions progress with the map and preserve their relative geographical arrangement; no visible teleport, unit cluster collision or text occlusion.
units_and_occlusion.readability_warning: Original full-body infantry are substantially smaller and less immediately identifiable on mobile than reference badges. Faction clothing accent is subtle. They do not equal the concept target volumetric 3D unit appearance.
units_and_occlusion.shore_warning: A few retained approximate reference anchors sit close to native coastal edges; this review does not certify survey-grade unit-coast contact.

hierarchy_and_rhythm.dead_time: No obvious isolated idle section; northward territorial change and camera tracking continue through frames 0-149.
hierarchy_and_rhythm.mobile_assessment: Territorial change is readable without text. Unit identity and luminous-front emphasis remain subdued at small viewing scale.
hierarchy_and_rhythm.camera: Continuous pan/zoom/roll visually tracks the front. No obvious hard cut or black corner in the contact sequence; exact georeferenced camera identity is not claimed.

remaining_design_gaps: Terrain relief is less aggressively lumpy than first prototype but retains a coarse embossed appearance and does not equal the concept target natural multiscale relief/ambient golden lighting.
Sea coastline rim is substantially reduced but sea imagery remains a stylized source-derived material, not concept-level natural water detail.
Front shape remains coarser than actual reference and luminous emphasis is subtler than the desired polished design direction.
Small flat original infantry remain less readable and volumetric than desired; their originality is separate from visual-quality equivalence.
